headline: 2008 order changes an earlier order on federal contractors and hiring rules, likely adding electronic work-eligibility checks.
what_it_does: This order changes Executive Order 12989, a 1996 order that bars the federal government from contracting with employers who knowingly hire workers not allowed to work in the US. Only the title was provided, so the exact changes are not confirmed here. This order is widely known for directing agencies to require federal contractors to use an electronic system, such as E-Verify, to check whether their workers can legally work in the US.

who_it_affects.how: They may be required to use an electronic system to confirm that their employees are allowed to work in the US.
Their work eligibility may be checked through an electronic government database.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed June 6, 2008; the source material gives no specific effective date.
